title: Papaya Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Papaya Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Papaya nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and boron in papaya, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Papaya nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your papaya turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, boron, magnesium, calcium, phosphorus and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Papaya leaf turning yellow then brown along the edges, a potassium shortage sign on older leaves

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, magnesium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron, calcium and zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which papaya nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a papaya nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest papaya nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in papaya

The older, lower leaves turn pale green to light green first, often starting at the leaf tip. New leaves come out smaller and less often, so the crown looks thin. Leaf stalks stay short, thin and pressed together, and may show a pinkish color. The tree grows slowly and sets fewer fruit. You see it most at this stage: any stage, but most often in fast growing young trees and in bearing trees that carry many fruit.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in papaya

Papaya feeds heavily and fruits all year, so it runs short fast when it is not fed every month or two. Sandy soils, heavy rain that washes nitrogen down, and soils low in organic matter make it worse.
How to tell it apart

Papaya ringspot virus also makes trees pale and slow. But it gives a yellow mosaic on young leaves, oily dark streaks on the leaf stalks and stem, and ring spots on the fruit. To be sure, do a soil test to see how short the soil is, as Kerala Agricultural University advises. A leaf test of recently matured leaves, blade and stalk, helps.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply a quick nitrogen fertilizer such as Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 around the tree, based on the soil test, and water it in. For a fast boost, Kerala Agricultural University gives a urea leaf spray of 10 grams per liter every 15 days. TNAU gives a stronger 2 percent spray (20 grams per liter), so try the milder rate first. Add compost or well rotted manure as well.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, feed in small, regular splits.
Potassium deficiency in papaya

blocks.alt: Papaya leaf turning yellow then brown along the edges, a potassium shortage sign on older leaves
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson, CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: The older, lower leaves show pale to lemon yellow edges first. The leaf tips and edges then die and turn brown, and new leaves come smaller. Purplish brown patches appear at the base of the leaf stalks. The whole tree can yellow early and grow much less, and the fruit are misshapen, poorly filled and hard to sell. You see it most at this stage: mostly in bearing trees, since the fruit pull a lot of potash out of the leaves.
Why potassium deficiency happens in papaya

Bearing trees need a steady supply of potash for the fruit. Sandy soils, acid soils below pH 6 (Kerala Agricultural University notes potash is taken up best above pH 6), heavy rain and feeding nitrogen without potash bring it on.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium shortage also hits old leaves, but the yellow runs between the veins and leaves green bands along the edge and midrib. While potash shortage scorches the edge itself. To be sure, do a soil test for potash, and test magnesium and calcium with it since they compete. A leaf test of the leaf stalks helps.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 around the tree based on the soil test, split into several doses, as Kerala Agricultural University advises. For quick help, KAU gives a Sulfate of potash leaf spray at 10 grams per liter with a sticker, sprayed in the morning. TNAU gives a 2 percent potassium chloride spray. On acid soil, bring the pH above 6 with Agricultural lime or Dolomite, and add organic matter.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash in every split along with nitrogen once the tree starts to bear.
Boron deficiency in papaya

blocks.alt: Row of papaya fruits that grow lumpy and misshapen from boron shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson (photo by Wayne Nishijima), CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Young fruit start to bleed latex and lose their shape, and the bumps grow worse as the fruit gets older. Parts of the fruit stop growing while the rest keeps swelling, so the fruit turns lumpy. Small cracks may ooze drops of latex, ripening is uneven, and seeds inside are aborted or poorly formed. In bad cases new leaves cup inward and turn brittle, the top bunches up, and the growing point can die. You see it most at this stage: fruiting. Signs start on young fruit and show most on mature fruit. It can come and go with the season.
Why boron deficiency happens in papaya
Heavy rain washes boron out of tropical soils. Shallow, rocky soils, dry spells and high pH soils also keep boron from the roots.
How to tell it apart

Papaya ringspot virus marks the fruit with dark rings and the leaves with a yellow mosaic. But the fruit stays round, while boron shortage makes real lumps. To be sure, send leaf stalks from healthy and sick trees of the same age to a lab. Hawaii CTAHR reports that trees with deformed fruit have about 20 ppm boron or less in the leaf stalk.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Hawaii CTAHR reports that a 0.25 percent borax spray (2.5 grams per liter) on the leaves, or 1 to 3 kg of boron (not borax) per hectare on the ground, raised boron and cleared the next fruit. Kerala Agricultural University gives 4 grams of Borax per tree in the soil, or a spray of 1 gram per liter. Fruit set after the treatment comes out normal in about three months. Boron turns toxic easily, so never go above these rates.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add compost every season, since boron comes with organic matter.
Magnesium deficiency in papaya

The bottom leaves yellow between the veins first, while a band of green stays around the edge and beside the midrib. Later the yellow moves in from the edge toward the midrib and brown spots form on the edges. Leaf stalks show purplish mottling, leaves can be misshapen, and trees stay shorter. You see it most at this stage: mostly in bearing trees and after heavy potash feeding.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in papaya
Acid, sandy soils that have lost magnesium to rain, and heavy potash use, which crowds magnesium out.
How to tell it apart

Potash shortage also starts on old leaves. But it scorches the edge itself and puts purplish brown patches at the base of the leaf stalk. To be sure, do a soil test, as Kerala Agricultural University advises, and check magnesium, potash and calcium together. A leaf test helps.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Kerala Agricultural University gives 32 grams of Magnesium sulfate per tree, laid in a band near the tree. For a quick fix, TNAU gives a Magnesium sulfate leaf spray at 1 to 2 percent (10 to 20 grams per liter). Do not apply magnesium and potash fertilizer at the same time.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use Dolomite instead of plain lime on acid soils.
Calcium deficiency in papaya

The growing tip and the young leaves show it first. New leaves turn pale with curled edges, and small dead spots spread over the blade so the leaves do not grow well. Leaf stalks can twist and fold, the space between leaves shortens so the top looks bunched, and the fruit flesh goes soft. You see it most at this stage: fast growth and fruit development.
Why calcium deficiency happens in papaya
Acid soils low in calcium, and too much phosphorus. Boron shortage can also bring on calcium shortage, since the plant needs boron to use calcium.
How to tell it apart

Boron shortage also hits young leaves and the top, and the two often come together. But boron shortage shows most as lumpy fruit that bleed latex. To be sure, do a soil test with pH, since acid soils point to low calcium. A leaf test helps, and test boron at the same time.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

On acid soil, Kerala Agricultural University gives Agricultural lime at 300 to 500 grams per tree per year. On soil that is not acid, use Gypsum, which adds calcium without raising pH. Correct boron shortage too. Calcium nitrate can also be used. Follow the label.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soil before planting, based on a soil test, and avoid too much phosphate fertilizer.
Phosphorus deficiency in papaya

The tree stops growing taller and makes fewer leaves. Leaves take on a dark or bluish green color. The older, lower leaves get uneven dead patches and yellow edges, and they die early. Roots grow poorly. You see it most at this stage: young trees after transplanting, and on poor acid soils.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in papaya
Acid soils and very alkaline soils hold phosphorus tight. Kerala Agricultural University notes it is taken up best between pH 6.2 and 7.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen shortage also stunts the tree, but its leaves are pale, not dark. Root rot and nematodes also stop growth, so pull a weak tree and look at the roots. To be sure, do a soil test for phosphorus and pH. A leaf test helps.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

For quick correction, Kerala Agricultural University advises Superphosphate 0 20 0. For the long term, bone meal or rock phosphate. Follow the soil test for the rate, as TNAU also advises. Mix organic manure with phosphate solubilizing bacteria to make more of it available.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphate fertilizer and compost in the planting hole, and keep soil pH between about 6.2 and 7 with lime.
Zinc deficiency in papaya

No detailed papaya description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. New leaves come out small and narrow and turn yellow between the veins, while the veins stay green. The space between leaves shortens so the top looks bunched, and fruit stay small. TNAU notes that zinc and boron shortage are common where papaya is grown on the same land year after year. You see it most at this stage: young leaves in any stage. Worst in fields that have grown papaya for several crops.
Why zinc deficiency happens in papaya
Fields cropped to papaya again and again, high pH soils, sandy soils and heavy phosphate use.
How to tell it apart

Papaya ringspot virus also makes young leaves small, mottled and twisted. But it brings a yellow mosaic, oily streaks on the stalks and ring spots on the fruit. To be sure, do a soil test with pH and a leaf test. Spray zinc on a few trees and see if the next leaves come out normal.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

TNAU reports that a leaf spray of 0.5 percent Zinc sulfate (5 grams per liter) together with 0.1 percent boron, given at the fourth and eighth month after planting, raised yield and fruit quality. Do not mix zinc with phosphate fertilizer in one dose.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, rotate papaya with other crops where you can, add compost.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any papaya nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your papaya needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Papaya nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my papaya leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: lower leaves go pale green from the tip, new leaves come small and slow, and leaf stalks are short, thin and pinkish. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in papaya?
items.a: Apply a quick nitrogen fertilizer such as Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 around the tree, based on the soil test, and water it in. For a fast boost, Kerala Agricultural University gives a urea leaf spray of 10 grams per liter every 15 days.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in papaya?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 around the tree based on the soil test, split into several doses, as Kerala Agricultural University advises. For quick help, KAU gives a Sulfate of potash leaf spray at 10 grams per liter with a sticker, sprayed in the morning.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes boron deficiency in papaya?
items.a: Hawaii CTAHR reports that a 0.25 percent borax spray (2.5 grams per liter) on the leaves, or 1 to 3 kg of boron (not borax) per hectare on the ground, raised boron and cleared the next fruit. Kerala Agricultural University gives 4 grams of Borax per tree in the soil, or a spray of 1 gram per liter.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my papaya lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the papaya nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
